description:
Pressure-test the ReqLlmNext v2 architecture across the two highest-value provider lanes we have in hand right now:
- Anthropic Messages models and beta features
- OpenAI Responses HTTP and WebSocket modes

Goals:
- expand provider/model coverage without collapsing concerns
- keep the happy path declarative and execution-plan-driven
- isolate edge cases into narrow policy rules or layer-scoped adapters
- use fixtures and careful live testing to surface architectural drift
- compare provider differences and fold the results back into the planning model

Testing posture:
- prefer replay first and targeted fixture recording second
- use curated anchor models instead of blasting the full catalog indiscriminately
- keep live API use deliberate, representative, and cost-aware

Desired outcome:
- confidence that the execution-plan spine stays simple for common cases
- explicit pressure-test evidence for the edge cases that require special handling
- a clearer map of what belongs in metadata, policy rules, surfaces, transports, and adapters

graph LR
    A[Catalog provider surfaces] --> B[Anthropic core support]
    B --> C[Anthropic beta and edge-case policy]

title: Pressure test Anthropic and OpenAI architecture lanes
